subject: HorizonWorks Private Deployment: implementation playbook + network Q&A
messages:
From: camila.reyes@redwood.com
To: aisha.patel@horizonworks.com, carlos.mendes@horizonworks.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: HorizonWorks Private Deployment: kickoff items and network inventory request

Hi Aisha / Carlos,

Great to meet you both on the call earlier. I've pasted a short checklist below to get the Private deployment (VPC peering + private endpoints + on-prem package) into our implementation sprint. Can you confirm the items you can share this week?

- Network inventory (CIDRs, VPC names, account IDs) - CSV preferred
- Intended peering model (AWS Transit Gateway, VPC Peering, or dedicated interconnect)
- Private endpoint requirements (internal-only domains, TLS termination point)
- Appliance footprint: expected rack power, public-facing management IPs (if any)
- Preferred maintenance windows and cutover blackout windows (timezone)

If you can attach the inventory, I’ll convert it into our playbook and share a draft M.A.P. (mutual action plan) for signoff.

I’ve looped in Laura for networking handoff and Marcus for on-prem appliance ops.

Thanks,

--
Camila Reyes
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@horizonworks.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com
Cc: aisha.patel@horizonworks.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HorizonWorks Private Deployment: kickoff items and network inventory request

Camila,

Thanks — attaching our network inventory (hw-network-inventory.csv). Summary highlights:
- Primary account: hw-prod-001 (us-east-1) | CIDR: 10.8.0.0/16
- Secondary account (staging): hw-stg-002 | CIDR: 10.9.0.0/16
- We currently use a Transit Gateway for cross-account routing; we'd prefer Transit Gateway peering to avoid additional BGP config on our side.
- We will allocate a dedicated /28 for the Redwood private endpoints (suggested range: 10.8.255.240/28)
- Management plane is currently NAT'd behind a bastion (no public management IPs planned)

Notes on compliance: we need to ensure KMS key usage is scoped; Aisha will follow up with the specific KMS CMKs.

Carlos

Attachment: hw-network-inventory.csv (CSV, 12 rows)

---

From: camila.reyes@redwood.com
To: carlos.mendes@horizonworks.com, aisha.patel@horizonworks.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood playbook draft + proposed cutover cadence (v0.1)

Hi team,

Thanks for the inventory, Carlos — that helps a lot. I’ve drafted a short implementation playbook (redwood-private-playbook-v0.1.pdf) and a high-level schedule below. Major assumptions are listed so we can quickly iterate.

Playbook highlights (summary):
1) Preflight (week -2)
   - Validate CIDR overlaps (Redwood infra team)
   - Confirm TGW attachment and route propagation rules
   - Exchange peering account IDs and authorization tokens
2) Network setup (week -1)
   - Create Redwood-side TGW attachment in us-east-1
   - Provision private endpoints (dedicated /28) and internal DNS records
   - Configure security groups and NACLs: allow 443 (TLS) and 50051 (gRPC) from HorizonWorks CIDRs
3) Appliance install (day 0)
   - Rack & power verification, IP assignment for management NIC (internal-only)
   - Bring up appliance in isolated staging with sample workload
4) Cutover & validation (day 2 - 4)
   - Canary traffic via header-based routing to validate latency and tokens
   - Perf run with 95th p99 token latency targets (Redwood provided harness)

Assumptions listed: Transit Gateway peering preferred; KMS CMK exchange for envelope encryption; no public management IPs required.

Proposed dates (please confirm):
- Preflight: Oct 18 - Oct 22
- Network setup: Oct 25 - Oct 29
- Appliance install window: Nov 1 - Nov 3
- Cutover: Nov 8 - Nov 9

Action items:
- HorizonWorks: confirm /28 allocation and share CMK ARN for KMS integration (Aisha)
- Redwood: provide detailed firewall rule table and appliance rack manifest (Marcus)
- Both: DocuSign for PO + deployment SOW (Laura will share the link)

Thanks — I’ll incorporate feedback and circulate M.A.P.

Best,

--
Camila Reyes
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-private-playbook-v0.1.pdf (PDF, 8 pages)

---

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com, carlos.mendes@horizonworks.com, aisha.patel@horizonworks.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood playbook draft + proposed cutover cadence (v0.1)

Carlos / Aisha — quick technical clarifications from the networking side:

- Please confirm whether the Transit Gateway is in a shared services account or owned by prod account (hw-prod-001). We need to know who will attach the Redwood TGW and who manages route propagation.
- We recommend letting Redwood create the TGW attachment and we’ll hand back the attachment ID; this reduces time to provision.
- IP plan: the suggested /28 for private endpoints is fine, but please ensure the .240-.255 range is not used in any on-prem NAT translations.
- Firewall rules (minimum):
   * 443/TCP inbound from 10.8.0.0/16 (for API TLS)
   * 50051/TCP inbound from 10.8.0.0/16 (gRPC internal)
   * 123/UDP NTP outbound allowed to our NTP IPs for appliance clock sync
- If HorizonWorks wants mutual TLS termination at their side, we’ll need the client cert CNs and a CA bundle prior to cutover.

I'll draft a one-page network runbook stub and paste it into the M.A.P.

Laura
Network Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

---

From: aisha.patel@horizonworks.com
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2027 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood playbook draft + proposed cutover cadence (v0.1)

Camila / Laura / Marcus,

Thanks for the draft. A couple of items on security / compliance:
- KMS: we will not share the CMK key material. Instead, we will create an IAM role for Redwood to use for envelope encryption within our account (role ARN will be provided by Oct 20).
- HSM: for now HSM is not required; however, we need to keep the option open if regulatory asks arise. Please confirm the on-prem package supports HSM-backed signing for future firmware attestation.
- Audit logs: we need 90-day retention of call traces and admin actions forwarded to our Splunk instance (we will provide endpoint for log shipping).

Attachment: hw-questions-and-constraints.md (text, 1 page)

Also — can we schedule a 30-min engineering sync next week (Oct 20) to walk the TGW attachment steps? Prefer 10:00-12:00 ET.

Best,
Aisha Patel
VP, Cloud Ops | HorizonWorks

---

From: camila.reyes@redwood.com
